## Prance Jillette

**Who is he?** A red-coated Earth-pony stallion with a teal mane, tail and goatee, dark glasses, and (in the mobile game) a black suit and tie. He is a recognizable **Penn Jillette lookalike** in the Las Pegasus crowd, paired with the smaller, Teller-inspired pony fans call **Josehoof Teller**. They are pony caricatures of the magicians, **not secret identities** of those real people.

**Names and continuity.** *Prance Jillette* is a **fandom name**, rather than a confirmed name spoken in *Friendship Is Magic*. A [2016 episode follow-up](https://www.equestriadaily.com/2016/09/viva-las-pegasus-episode-followup.html?variant=318122597795) recognized the two as Penn-and-Teller references without using those pony names. The licensed Gameloft game calls him **Skeptical Magician Pony** and his companion **Silent Magician Pony**. Its biography gives Prance a stage career and a fondness for exposing hoaxes with his quiet best friend; that is **game characterization**, not an established television plotline. See the [character and appearance index](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_ponies/Earth_ponies/Stallions) and [mobile-game character listing](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/My_Little_Pony_Friendship_is_Magic_Wiki%3AWorkshop/List_of_My_Little_Pony_%28mobile_game%29_characters/Ponyville_%28M-Z%29).

**Where to spot him.** He debuts among the guests of Gladmane's resort in **“Viva Las Pegasus” (S6E20)** and returns as background scenery in **“Grannies Gone Wild” (S8E5)**; he is also cataloged in **“Baby Flurry Heart's Heartfelt Scrapbook,” episode 8**. **Speaking:** no verified dialogue or credited voice actor in the show.

1. **The magician-duo Easter egg — “Viva Las Pegasus” (S6E20).** His appearance alongside the Teller lookalike establishes the recognizable celebrity homage; he has no verified part in resolving the episode's conflict. 2. **A little personality beyond the cameo — *My Little Pony: Magic Princess* (mobile game; no season/episode).** The **Skeptical Magician Pony** promotion describes a stage performer who enjoys debunking misconceptions with his quiet partner; this is his clearest published characterization, not a television scene. **Video timestamp unavailable.**

There are no verified dialogue-driven or plot-changing scenes for this background stallion; the later screen appearances are cameos rather than additional character-defining moments.
